newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to offers Asia's first Internet TV.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to offers Asia's first Internet TV.

text.p: Singapore said on Friday it would soon offer Asia's first Internet access to services offering video as good as television.
Singapore Telecom (SingTel) and the Television Corporation of Singapore (TCS) said in a statement a trial of the service would start in 40 homes in March.
In June, a three-month commerical trial will start in 300 homes, with TCS providing the contents and SingTel providing the network and infrastructure for delivery.
Internet users will be able to download "full motion video" rather than the jerky, out-of-synch pictures now available.

Users require a special modem called Asymmetrical Digital Subscriber Lines delivering data to a home computer at 6.0 megabytes per second (Mbps) compared to the 28.8 kilobytes per second (kps) of an ordinary modem.
Customers will receive films, film previews, educational material, music videos and games, the statement said.
It did not say how much the service would cost.
